one_line: A 35-second narrated moral story about two friends, Tom and Tim, and a chocolate bar, told with a new AI-generated painterly image every 1.5 to 3 seconds and yellow burned-in word captions.

hook.visual: Painterly aerial view of a small village with a dirt road and green fields (0.0 s), then a lakeside village at 1.5 s and two boys seen from behind walking down a sunlit alley at 3.0 s.
hook.on_screen_text: VILLAGE (1.5 s), FRIENDS (3.0 s) in bold yellow capitals, one word at a time. (Nothing on screen at 0.0 s.)
hook.first_spoken_line: Once upon a time, in a little village, there lived two friends named Tom and Tim. (Whisper, 0.0 to 4.8 s)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Observed: lush, warm illustrated scenery and big yellow captions from the first 2 s. Weak spot: there is no conflict or question until the chocolate bar at about 10 s. Inferred: 'Once upon a time' works as a bedtime-story cue for the kids and parents who search for it.

beats.observed: Four different illustrated scenes: an aerial village (0.0 s), a lakeside village (1.5 s), a sunlit alley with two boys seen from behind (3.0 s), two boys shaking hands (4.5 s), a boy at a tree-house window with another boy below (6.0 s), two boys sitting playing with small objects (7.5 s).

payoff: The apology and the closing moral 'sharing brings happiness and friendship', from about 29 s to the end at 35 s.
cta: none in the video. The caption is a description only, with no ask.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: a parent sends or saves a 35 s moral story about sharing for a child. Comment count is not provided in meta.json.
why_it_worked: 3,896,934 views is 169x the account's median of 23,000 (meta.json). Caution: the video was uploaded on 2023-06-21 (meta.json), so the views have accumulated over more than 3 years.
72,104 likes at 1.85% is the highest like rate of the three videos in this batch. Inferred: a short, clean moral story is easy for parents to approve of and for children to watch to the end.
Observed: a new image every 1.5 to 3 s with one yellow word at a time on screen keeps the screen changing for the full 35 s, and the moral lands in the last 6 s. This is an easy-to-copy structure.
paid_signal: no, inferred: like_rate 1.85% is well above the 0.3% paid-pattern line and there is no sign of promotion.

solo_route.how: 1) Write an 80 to 90 word Hebrew story of 7 to 8 sentences about one developmental theme (sharing, trying again, a first day), with the child hero's name. 2) Generate 10 to 12 stills, one per sentence, ALL from LumeBook's own illustrated hero as the reference so the child looks the same in every scene (this video shows five different 'Toms' and 'Tims'). 3) Animate each still with a slow push-in or a short image-to-video clip of 2 to 3 s. 4) Add an AI Hebrew voice-over, then burned-in Hebrew captions in CapCut with one highlighted word at a time, in a bold color. 5) End on a LumeBook title card. About 35 s. About 2 to 3 hours.
solo_route.needs: Nothing for a fictional hero. Any claim about at what age children learn to share needs a barter child-development expert or a source. Use an AI voice that is not cloned from a real person and check the tool's commercial-use terms.

lumebook_version.hook_he: בן 4 ולא רוצה לחלוק? סיפור של 30 שניות
lumebook_version.concept: A 30 to 35 s illustrated Hebrew story about the LumeBook hero learning to share a snack, with one consistent hero across all stills, a word-by-word captioned voice-over, and a closing card showing the same hero on a LumeBook cover.

evidence_notes: Observed AI cues: no consistent character: Tom and Tim look different in nearly every shot, with different hair, face shape and clothes (a black-haired boy in a grey shirt at 13.5 to 16.5 s, brown-haired toddlers at 18.0 to 25.5 s, a suspender-wearing boy at 27.0 to 28.5 s, two boys in a shack at 30.0 to 31.5 s, two small children in overalls at 33.0 to 34.5 s). Image style also changes between shots: photoreal aerial, oil-paint style, and a smoother semi-realistic render. At 9.0 and 10.5 s a chocolate bar is wedged in a tree trunk with a dark red cavity, which makes no physical sense. The wrapper pile at 18.0 and 19.5 s looks like repeated, fused tiles. Faces are smooth and slightly waxy, and the fingers holding wrappers at 13.5 to 16.5 s are simplified and blurred together. Several shots look like a still with a slow push-in (13.5, 15.0 and 16.5 s are the same image at slightly different scale). Others show real movement (the children's legs and arms change position between 33.0 and 34.5 s). Tool: the caption and description name no tool. meta.json notes the title ends with 'AI', but the caption field does not contain the title, so I cannot confirm it. I cannot tell which tool made it. A tiny watermark-like handle sits at the bottom of the 9.0 and 10.5 s frames [unclear, unreadable at this size]; inferred: that one image may have come from a generator account or another source. Transcript: clear narration that matches the caption's story and the shots, so reliability is high; the burned-in word 'OLD.' at 25.5 s has no matching word in the transcript (Whisper has 'small piece and smiled'). I cannot hear the voice, so I do not say whether it is an AI voice. made_by brand_inhouse means only that the channel uploaded it. Likeness and consent: only invented children; no real child or celebrity look-alike is apparent. LumeBook-specific risk: if its hero is a customer's child, use only that family's consent-approved image, never a real child's photo in an ad without written parental consent, and no voice cloned from a real person.
